items.body: A company runs an employee suggestion system that rewards suggestions bringing substantial cost reduction, and its manager uses 'we' instead of 'I' in all conversations with workers. Which Fayol principle is reflected in the manager's practice?

options.text: Initiative
Esprit de corps
Unity of direction
Centralisation

excerpts.text:
(xiii)Initative: Workers should be
encouraged to develop and carry
out their plans for improvements
according to Fayol. Initiative
means taking the first step with
self-motivation. It is thinking
out and executing the plan. It is
one of the traits of an intelligent
person. Initiative should be
encouraged. But it does not mean
going against the established
practices of the company for
the sake of being different. A
good company should have an
employee suggestion system
whereby initiative/suggestions
which result in substantial
cost/time reduction should be
rewarded.
(xiv) Esprit De Corps: Management
should promote a team spirit
of unity and harmony among
employees, according to Fayol.
Management should promote
teamwork especially in large
organisations because otherwise
objectives would be difficult to
realise. It will also result in a
loss of coordination. A manager
should replace ‘I’ with ‘We’ in all
his conversations with workers
to foster team spirit. This will
give rise to a spirit of mutual
trust and belongingness among
team members. It will also
minimise the need for using
penalties.

items.proposed_explanation: Replacing 'I' with 'We' fosters team spirit, mutual trust and belongingness among team members, which is esprit de corps. Unity of direction and centralisation are not described in the case.

frozen_blind.source_explanation: F3 ties the employee suggestion system rewarding cost reduction to Initiative and replacing 'I' with 'We' to Esprit de corps. The stem contains both, so A and B are each partly correct and there is no single answer. C and D are unsupported by F3.

items.body: Anil Ltd raises a larger share of its capital through debt instead of equity, and its cost of equity remains unaffected. Which statement is correct as per the textbook discussion of debt?

options.text: The overall cost of capital is likely to rise, because debt is costlier than equity
The overall cost of capital is likely to fall, but fixed financial charges and financial risk increase
Financial risk falls, because payment of interest and return of principal is not obligatory
Financial risk remains unchanged, because equity is considered riskless for the business

excerpts.text:
is likely to lower the over-all cost of
capital of the firm provided that the
cost of equity remains unaffected.
Impact of a change in the debt-equity
ratio upon the earning per share is
dealt with in detail later in this chapter.
Debt is cheaper but is more risky
for a business because the payment of
interest and the return of principal is
obligatory for the business. Any default
in meeting these commitments may
force the business to go into liquidation.
There is no such compulsion in case of
equity, which is therefore, considered
riskless for the business. Higher use
of debt increases the fixed financial
charges of a business. As a result,
increased use of debt increases the
financial risk of a company.
Financial risk is the chance that
a firm would fail to meet its payment
obligations.
Capital structure of a company,
thus, affects both the profitability and
the financial risk. A capital structure
will be said to be optimal when the
proportion of debt and equity is
such that it results in an increase
in the value of the equity share. In
other words, all decisions relating to
capital structure should emphasise on
increasing the shareholders’ wealth.
The proportion of debt in the overall
capital is also called financial leverage.

items.proposed_explanation: The excerpt says higher debt is likely to lower the overall cost of capital if the cost of equity is unaffected, since debt is cheaper. It also says higher use of debt increases fixed financial charges and therefore financial risk. Option C is contradicted because payment of interest and return of principal is obligatory, and option D because increased use of debt increases financial risk.

frozen_blind.source_explanation: F15 states more debt is likely to lower overall cost of capital provided cost of equity is unaffected, but it raises fixed financial charges and financial risk. A reverses the cost claim. C contradicts the obligatory interest and principal payment. D contradicts that debt increases financial risk.

items.body: A firm sends its employees to a three-week programme that builds their skills and knowledge. Which term best describes the programme?

options.text: Education
Development
Selection
Training

excerpts.text:
are distinct terms although they
overlap to some extent.
Training is any process by which
the aptitudes, skills and abilities
of employees to perform specific
jobs are increased. It is a process of
learning new skills and application
of knowledge. It attempts to
improve their performance on the
current job or prepare them for any
intended job.
Education is the process of increa­
sing the knowledge and understanding
of employees. It is the understanding
and interpretation of knowledge. It
does not provide definite answers, but
rather develops a logical and rational
mind that can determine relationships
among pertinent variables and
thereby understand a phenomenon.
Education imparts qualities of mind
and character and understanding of
the basic principles and develop the
capacities of analysis, synthesis and
objectivity. Education is broader in
scope than training. Training is tied
to the goals of organisations more
than to the goals of the individual.
Development refers to the
learning opportunities designed
to help employees grow. It covers
not only those activities which
improve job performance but also
those which bring about growth of
the personality, help individuals
in the progress towards maturity
and actualisation of their potential

items.proposed_explanation: Training increases the aptitudes, skills and abilities of employees, and it is a process of learning new skills and application of knowledge. The programme builds skills and knowledge, so it is training.

frozen_blind.source_explanation: F12 defines training as improving skills for specific jobs, education as knowledge and understanding, and development as growth opportunities, and says they overlap. The stem gives no job-specific or growth cue, so Training and Development are both arguable. Selection is unrelated.

items.body: Smita plans her Diwali collection in June, then continuously monitors whether production proceeds according to plan and briefs the marketing department in time. Which feature of coordination does this illustrate?

options.text: Coordination is a continuous process
Coordination is an all pervasive function
Coordination is a one-time function performed at the planning stage
Coordination is required only at the top level of management

excerpts.text:
the goals of the organisation.
At Namchi Designer Candles,
the production and sales
department have to coordinate
their work, so that production
takes place according to the
demand in the market.
(iii) Coordination is a continuous
process: Coordination is not
a one-time function but a
continuous process. It begins at
the planning stage and continues
till controlling. Smita plans her
dewali collection in the month
of June itself. She has to then
ensure that there is adequate
workforce and continuously
monitor whether production is
proceeding according to plans.
Her marketing department also
has to be briefed in time to
prepare their promotional and
advertising campaigns.
(iv) Coordination is an all pervasive
function: Coordination is required
at all levels of management due
to the interdependent nature of
activities of various departments.
It integrates the efforts of different
departments and different levels.
The purchase, production and
sales departmental efforts have
to be coordinated by Smita for
achieving organisational objectives
harmoniously. The purchase
department is responsible for
procuring fabric. This then
becomes the basis of the activities
of the production department

items.proposed_explanation: Smita has to align efforts of several departments, which shows that coordination is required at all levels because of the interdependence of activities. This makes it an all pervasive function.

frozen_blind.source_explanation: F1 (iii) uses the same Smita example for coordination as a continuous process, beginning at planning and continuing through monitoring. B concerns levels and departments (F1 iv), not shown here. C and D contradict F1.

items.body: A regional sales head fixes a permissible limit for monthly expense variance. Only deviations that cross this limit are brought to her attention, and routine problems are left to subordinates. Which consequence of this approach is established by the textbook?

options.text: Managers must personally examine every deviation, so more managerial time is consumed
Delegation of authority becomes harder, because subordinates handle routine problems
Managerial time is saved and attention is focused on important areas
Employee morale falls, because routine problems are left to subordinates

excerpts.text:
When a manager sets critical points and focuses attention on significant deviations which
cross the permissible limit, the following advantages accrue:
1. It saves the time and efforts of managers as they deal with only significant deviations.
2. It focuses managerial attention on important areas. Thus, there is better utilisation of
managerial talent.
3. The routine problems are left to the subordinates. Management by exception, thus,
facilitates delegation of authority and increases morale of the employees.
4. It identifies critical problems which need timely action to keep the organisation in right
track.

items.proposed_explanation: Dealing only with significant deviations saves the time and efforts of managers and focuses managerial attention on important areas, so there is better utilisation of managerial talent. The excerpt says leaving routine problems to subordinates facilitates delegation of authority and increases morale, which contradicts options B and D. Option A is contradicted since managers deal with only significant deviations.

frozen_blind.source_explanation: F14 lists saved time and effort and focus on important areas as advantages of dealing only with deviations beyond the permissible limit. A, B and D reverse F14's statements that time is saved, delegation is facilitated and morale rises.

items.body: A firm obtains (i) finance from financiers, (ii) pays taxes to the government, (iii) draws power and water, and (iv) pays a return on financial investment to its investors. Using the textbook's classification of inputs and outputs, which two are outputs supplied by the enterprise to its environment?

options.text: (i) and (iii)
(i) and (ii)
(ii) and (iii)
(ii) and (iv)

excerpts.text:
measures as improving the
quality of the product, reducing
cost of the production, engaging
in aggr essive advertising, and
so on.
(iii) It helps in tapping useful
resources: Environment is a
source of various resources
for running a business.
To engage in any type of
activity, a business enterprise
assembles various resources
called inputs like finance,
machines, raw materials,
power and water, labour, etc.,
from its environment including
financiers, government and
suppliers. They decide to provide
these resources with their own
expectations to get something in
return from the enterprise. The
business enterprise supplies the
environment with its outputs
such as goods and services for
customers, payment of taxes to
government, return on financial
investment to investors and
so on. Because the enterprise
depends on the environment as
a source of inputs or resources
and as an outlet for outputs,
it only makes sense that the
enterprise designs policies that
allow it to get the resources
that it needs so that it can
convert those resources into
outputs that the environment
desires. This can be done better
by understanding what the
environment has to offer.

items.proposed_explanation: The enterprise assembles inputs like finance, machines, raw materials, power and water, labour from its environment. It supplies outputs such as goods and services, payment of taxes to government, and return on financial investment to investors. So (ii) and (iv) are outputs, while (i) and (iii) are inputs, and each of options A, B and C includes at least one of these inputs.

frozen_blind.source_explanation: F6 lists finance, power and water as inputs, and goods and services, taxes to government and return on investment to investors as outputs. Hence (ii) and (iv) are outputs; A, B and C each include an input.

items.body: Using the definitions by Chester Barnard and Keith Davis, which statement about an informal organisation is correct?

options.text: It is established by the formal organisation to define authority relationships among activities
It exists only when its relationships contribute to joint results
It is created through a conscious purpose set by management
It arises spontaneously as people associate with one another, without being established or required by the formal organisation

excerpts.text:
Organising is the process of identifying and grouping the work to
be performed, defining and delegating responsibility and authority,
and establishing relationships for the purpose of enabling people to
work most effectively together in accomplishing objectives.
Louis Allen
Organising is the process of defining and grouping the activities of the
enterprise and establishing authority relationships among them.
Theo Haimman

An informal organisation is an aggregate of interpersonal relationships without any
conscious purpose but which may contribute to joint results.
Chester Barnand
Informal organisation is a network of personal and social relations not established or required
by the formal organisation but arising spontaneously as people associate with one another.
Keith Davis

items.proposed_explanation: Keith Davis describes informal organisation as a network of personal and social relations not established or required by the formal organisation but arising spontaneously as people associate. Barnard says it is without any conscious purpose and that it only 'may' contribute to joint results, so options B and C are contradicted. Defining activities and establishing authority relationships is Haimman's definition of organising, not of informal organisation, which rules out A.

frozen_blind.source_explanation: F10: Davis describes spontaneous personal and social relations not established or required by the formal organisation; Barnard says without conscious purpose. A and C contradict this, and B turns Barnard's 'may contribute' into 'only when'.

items.proposed_explanation: The incentive is 1,800 x 4 = Rs 7,200, so the total is 10,000 + 7,200 = Rs 17,200. The fixed monthly salary is time based and the per-unit amount is performance based, so the plan combines time based pay with incentives. Options B and C count only one component, and option D is contradicted because salaries and incentives are direct financial payments.

frozen_blind.source_explanation: Total pay is 10,000 + 7,200 = Rs 17,200. F11 describes a combination of time based pay plus incentives for higher performance as a direct payment plan. B and C ignore part of the pay, and D misclassifies direct pay as indirect.
